terms.gloss: have in mind, plan, intend (+ infinitive)
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 52: istum exhērēdāre in animō habēbat (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: I have it in mind (+ infinitive)
evidence: Cic. Fam. (Lewis & Short s.v. animus): nōbīs erat in animō Cicerōnem ad Caesarem mittere

terms.comment: Classically “stretch, aim, direct”; with an infinitive “intend” it is chiefly Livy’s.

sources: Lewis & Short: animus · Lewis & Short: intendo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 360.
